name: Aider
description: Tier B capture: overrides Aider's shell via AIDER_SHELL_CMD so every command Aider spawns is bracketed with command_start / command_end events on RedLog's timeline.
author: your-handle

capture.name: Aider (SHELL wrapper)
capture.description: Wraps every shell command Aider spawns so it lands in the RedLog timeline as an agent event.

manualSteps.label: Point Aider's shell override at the wrapper. Add this to your shell rc (~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc)
Reload your shell so AIDER_SHELL_CMD is visible to newly launched Aider sessions
Smoke-test: this should print 'hello' AND create a command_start/command_end pair on the RedLog timeline
Run Aider normally — every tool call should now be tagged 'aider-wrapper' in the timeline

NOTE — the exact env var name for Aider's shell override may differ between releases. This plugin assumes AIDER_SHELL_CMD invoked as `$AIDER_SHELL_CMD -c '<command>'`. Confirm against https://aider.chat/docs/config/options.html#--shell before relying on this in a real engagement; if Aider uses a different flag or arg style, adjust the export accordingly.
